findings.body: The user provider receives authorization-resource UUIDs instead of realm group IDs, so its group-membership query matches no users and authorized group-member searches/counts omit the permitted users.
findings.failure_mode: Group-scoped member permissions do not produce the group IDs consumed by user search and count filtering.
findings.impact: The user provider receives authorization-resource UUIDs instead of realm group IDs, so its group-membership query matches no users and authorized group-member searches/counts omit the permitted users.
findings.root_cause: The code confuses the authorization Resource ID with the represented GroupModel ID.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the group resource name (which is created from the realm group ID) rather than resource.getId(), or otherwise resolve each authorization resource back to its realm group ID before passing the set to user queries.
findings.title: Use the group identifier rather than the authorization resource identifier
findings.trigger: With admin fine-grained authorization V2 enabled, grant an administrator VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group and then search or count users through the admin API.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 123 `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` exists verbatim. The code adds the authorization Resource's internal ID, but consumers (JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery) expect realm GroupModel IDs. AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name, so the resource name equals the group ID, but groupResource.getId() is the Resource entity's primary key, not its name. This mismatch causes user queries to find no matching group memberships.

findings.trigger: A maintainer or implementer consults the contract for requireManageMembers when determining which authorization condition it enforces.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 133 Javadoc states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}` for requireManageMembers, but the method name and implementation (GroupPermissions.java:376-379) check canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. findings.verifier_reason: Line 145 shows `@return Stream of IDs` but the method signature at line 147 is `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. The return type documentation says Stream but the actual return type is Set, which is a documentation error introduced by this patch.

finding.failure_mode: Authorization escalates an all-groups read grant into write access for operations that do not have a specific group target.
finding.impact: A read-only all-groups grant is treated as management authority, allowing the administrator to create groups despite lacking the MANAGE scope.

finding.title: All-groups view permission authorizes group management
finding.trigger: An administrator has only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource and invokes an operation requiring groups().requireManage(), such as creating a top-level group.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that VIEW scope grants MANAGE authority is incorrect. Line 70 shows canManage() checks for VIEW or MANAGE, but canManage(GroupModel group) at line 79 only checks MANAGE scope. The global canManage() is used for operations without a specific group target (like listing), not for creating groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage() which uses canManage() - this is intentional design allowing VIEW holders to access the endpoint but not necessarily create. The evidence does not prove privilege escalation.

finding.title: V2 group permission resources are left behind when groups are deleted
finding.trigger: Run with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled without the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, create a V2 permission for a group, and delete that group.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch moves the listener registration inside the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check but does not remove cleanup functionality. The claim assumes V2 creates persistent per-group resources requiring cleanup, but the patch context shows V2 uses a different permission model (AdminPermissionsSchema). The evidence does not prove V2 creates resources that require the same GroupRemovedEvent cleanup as V1, and absence of V2-specific cleanup code in this patch is not proof of a defect.
